newsitem.title: USA: Babbitt to announce plan to revive aquatic habitat.
newsitem.headline: Babbitt to announce plan to revive aquatic habitat.

text.p: Interior Secretary Bruce Babbitt plans to unveil on Tuesday a new campaign funded with $5 million in federal and private grants to replenish aquatic habitat for native fish species in 14 states this year.

Ultimately the "Bring Back the Natives" campaign, coordinated by the Interior and Agriculture departments, aims to restore habitat on 283,000 miles of streams and 6.5 million acres of lakes on 70 percent of all federal lands, or some 462 million acres, the Interior Department said in a statement.
Babbitt was due to announce the program in a speech in Haines City, Fla., Tuesday.

Babbitt said the program would spur rural economic growth, reduce flood and fire damage, and steer rare and declining trout and salmon species -- including the official state fish of California, Nevada, Oregon, Washington and Alaska -- off the Endangered Species List.

"Every public nickel is matched by private dimes, every quarter is pumped directly into the local watershed, every dollar bill invested toward a self-sustaining native fishery yields a fiver for community businesses in that watershed," Babbitt said.
"Healthy fisheries reflect a healthy watershed -- this translates to economic prosperity," Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said in the statement.
